title: probabilistic routing cost scenarios and fallback tier notes
content:
Overview

This is a working doc for a probabilistic smart-routing cost model that explicitly models: fallback tiers, region-level spot availability, and mixed on-demand/spot blends. Purpose: capture a compact simulation scaffold and recommended knobs that product and backend can expose in the Console Optimize tab.

High-level idea
- Rather than deterministic 'try next tier if primary fails', we model each request class as a distribution over latency and success/capacity by tier/region/provider.
- Use those distributions to compute expected unit-cost, expected latency, and outage probability for a given routing policy.
- Allow policy parameters: primary tier, fallback sequence, spot bid aggressiveness (prob of eviction), region preference weight, and cost-sensitivity lambda.

Why probabilistic?
- Observed in infra logs: spot evictions and cross-region throttling are stochastic; one-off worst-case rules over-penalize or undercount savings.
- Gives a smoother knob to trade cost vs reliability.

Quick glossary
- Tier: an abstraction of capacity category (e.g., hosted-standard, dedicated-reserved, fallback-spot, warm-cache-reserve)
- EvictionRate: P(spot request preempted per minute) for a workload class in a region
- FailoverLatency: additional ms introduced when we need to route to fallback region/tier
- BlendPrice: weighted per-token price if we route partially to different backends (e.g., 70% primary, 30% fallback)

Simple simulation spec (pseudocode)
- Inputs (per workload class): rps, seq_len_dist (mean), primary_tier, fallback_sequence, region_weights, spot_eviction_rate_by_region, price_table
- For t in 1..N_sim_steps: sample request sequence length, sample whether primary handles (Bernoulli with p=1-eviction_rate_primary), if fail route to next fallback in sequence, accumulate tokens, latency = base_latency(tier) + failover_penalty_if_any
- Outputs: mean_cost_per_request, 95th_latency, P_request_exceeds_SLO, expected_tokens_billed (include duplicated tokens if re-try semantics bill twice)
Key assumptions to validate
- Billing semantics for retries: are retries billed fully? (TODO: confirm with billing team)
- Cache reuse across retries: does prefix/KV cache survive failover to a different region/tier? (likely cold-start cost in many cases)
- Eviction independence across requests vs correlated spikes: model both IID and correlated scenarios.

Example scenario (hand-run numbers)
- Workload: chat-streaming, avg seq=256 tokens, rps=12 (tail heavy), SLO=200ms p95
- Primary: region A spot (price 0.3 units/token, eviction 3%/min), base p95 latency 120ms
- Fallback1: region A on-demand (price 0.6 units/token, eviction 0), base p95 latency 150ms, failover penalty 40ms
- Fallback2: region B spot (price 0.25 units/token, eviction 5%/min), base p95 latency 170ms, extra cross-region penalty 60ms

Hand-sim outcome (approx):
- If primary stays: cost = 256 * 0.3 = 76.8 units/request; p95 latency 120ms
- If evicted and failover to Fallback1: cost ~ (attempted tokens billed?) 256*(0.3 + 0.6) = 230.4 if billed twice, latency ~ 120 + 40 + remote-setup = 200ms (close to SLO)
- Expected cost with 3% eviction: 0.97*76.8 + 0.03*230.4 = 82.6 units/request (~7.5% higher than always-on-demand baseline of 153.6)
- Observations: small eviction rates can still have outsized latency impact due to double billing + cold-starts.

Policy knobs and UX proposals for Console Optimize
- Cost-sensitivity slider (0..1): maps to lambda in objective E[cost] + lambda * outage_penalty. Default 0.3 for PLG users.
- Fallback sequencing editor: allow reordering, set max hops, and toggle "cache-keep-alive" hint for infra (attempt to preserve KV across failovers).
- Spot bid aggressiveness: numeric 0..100 representing how deep we go into spot pools; ties to expected eviction_rate used in sim.
- Region policy: prefer-same-region boolean; when on, add a penalty to cross-region routing in expectation calculation.
- "Simulate impact" button: runs a quick Monte Carlo (1k samples) and shows estimated cost delta, p95 latency delta, and worst-case outage frequency.

Metrics to collect and validate model parameters
- Per-region spot eviction events (time series), join with workload id -> compute per-workload eviction distribution
- Retry counts per request id and billing token duplication counts
- Cold-start token delta: tokens billed on retry vs unique tokens seen by model
- Failure-mode traces: trace ids where failover occurred and corresponding latency trace

Open implementation issues (engineering)
- Where to run the Monte Carlo? Lightweight client-side vs server-side. For Console, server-side sandboxed run makes more sense (we have infra and pricing tables).
- Data freshness: we need 1h/24h/7d sliding windows for eviction rates; allow customers to pick the horizon used in sim.
- Billing semantics overrides: allow customer to model optimistic "retries not billed" or pessimistic "full double bill" for planning.

Decision heuristics (recommendations for default policies)
- Low-latency interactive workloads: default to prefer-same-region on-demand as primary; spot only for bursts with max hops = 1.
- Cost-sensitive batch/embedding workloads: allow primary=global-spot with fallback to on-demand in another region; set spot-bid-aggressiveness high.
- Mixed-criticality: for a single tenant with both chat and nightly ingest, expose per-route policy templates.

Mini-experiment proposals (A/B)
1) Experiment A: customers who enable probabilistic sim + adopt recommended policy vs control that keeps previous deterministic policy. Measure 30d cost %, p95 latency, and failover events.
2) Experiment B: change Console default cost-sensitivity from 0.3 -> 0.5 and observe changes in customer-selected policies and upstream infra load (more on-demand usage?).

Quick TODOs / Next steps
- [ ] Validate billing retry semantics with finance (owner: Zoe Chen) - target 2025-03-06
- [ ] Prototype a small Monte Carlo sim in routing-sim repo (PR #89 is a starting point) - owner: Miguel - 2025-02-28
- [ ] Add per-region eviction dashboards to Console telemetry (SRE input needed) - owner: Ava - 2025-03-12
- [ ] UX mock for fallback-sequence editor in Console - owner: product-design - 2025-03-07

Notes to self / rough thoughts
- Consider a hybrid analytic + sampling approach: analytic for expected cost, sampling for tail SLO metrics. Cheaper to run for many customers.
- Add a "safety floor" for policy suggestions: never auto-propose >60% spot for chat routes unless customer explicitly opts-in.

Questions for discussion
- Should we model correlated evictions (e.g., regional spot drain) by a latent factor that impacts many requests simultaneously? I think yes for worst-case planning.
- If we show customers expected double-billing numbers, will that cause support churn? We should include a clear explanation and an "assumptions" toggle.

Appendix: small ascii sensitivity table (example outputs of a 1k-sample sim)
- columns: spot_eviction_rate | expected_cost_delta_vs_on-demand | p95_latency | outage_freq_per_1k
- rows:
 0.01 | +2.1% | 130ms | 2
 0.03 | +7.4% | 180ms | 7
 0.05 | +12.3% | 230ms | 14

End of draft. Keep this in product/optimize as a working doc; will refine after billing confirmation and a quick prototype run.
